claim: For the attractive critical XX chain Gibbs family with fixed public J,tau,B,g_->0 and unknown |lambda|<=B,g>=g_-, there are parameter-blind CPTP encoders and decoders, uniform over all L>=2, whose persistent archive dimension is independent of L and whose full trace-norm error is at most epsilon. At fixed public constants, log2 D=O((1+log(1/epsilon))^(3/2)); asymptotically this is O(log^(3/2)(1/epsilon)).
supplied_inputs: Public L, J, tau, B, g_-, and epsilon. Actual lambda and g are not supplied. No Lieb-Liniger limit is assumed.
proof: Use the supplied uniform all-sector energy theorem and half-temperature Jensen bound; compress ordered fermion coordinates to symmetric labeled modes through a contraction K_m; compare free Dirichlet mode energy by K_m^*HfreeK_m<=Hcrit; truncate number and mode tails; complete encoder and decoder failures to vacuum and use the unnormalized-success trace distance bound.
persistent_cost: D_large=1+binom(M+r,r), D_small=1+sum_{m=0}^{min(r,L0-2)}binom(L0-2,m), and one register of dimension max(D_large,D_small). Direct-sum number label and overflow are included.
other_costs: O(r log N) reversible workspace, N output spins, number/permutation ranking, controlled amplitudes, sine-transform synthesis, finite-rotation precision, and runtime are separate. No input Gibbs preparation or energy-preserving decoding is claimed.
evidence: Analytic audit in RESULT.txt. Source checks rerun successfully. Additional finite matrix replay at work/programmes/combinatorics_optimization/cycle3/newarchive_audit/check_archive_map.py covers all 21 sectors 1<=m<=S<=6; it is finite evidence only.
falsifier: A valid ordered-coordinate sector with K_m^*HfreeK_m not below Hcrit, an encoder/decoder completeness failure, an omitted mode/number loss term, or a Gibbs parameter choice violating the stated uniform energy budget.
scope_caveat: This is an achievable archive bound, not an optimal memory rate, Lieb-Liniger limit theorem, or energy-preserving code. The half-temperature step takes the separate all-sector theorem as input.
